questions.question: What core problems with manual attendance in university classrooms motivated the development of the Smart Attendance System, and what specific objectives were established to resolve them?
expected_points: Manual roll call wastes around 10 minutes per lecture.
Manual roll call enables proxy attendance and lacks real-time reporting.
Objectives include cutting attendance time to under 1 minute, eliminating proxy attendance, providing real-time teacher dashboards, and securing biometric data.

questions.question: In your literature review, why did you discard RFID cards, fingerprint scanners, and Haar cascade approaches in favor of a FaceNet-style embedding model?
expected_points: RFID cards can be shared, leaving proxy attendance unresolved.
Fingerprint scanners process only one student at a time, creating queues.
Haar cascades were fast but suffered from poor accuracy under variable lighting.
FaceNet-style embeddings map faces to a 128-dimensional space where identical faces cluster closely, offering high benchmark accuracy (>99% on LFW) in real time on mid-range GPUs.

questions.question: Describe the overall three-tier architecture of your system, specifying the responsibilities and technologies used in each tier.
expected_points: Capture tier runs on a classroom PC equipped with a 1080p camera capturing frames every two seconds.
Application tier is a Python Flask REST API performing face detection with MTCNN and face recognition.
Data tier is a MySQL database maintaining records of students, courses, sessions, and attendance.

questions.question: How does the proposed solution safeguard against quick spoofing attempts using held-up photos during live classroom sessions?
expected_points: Students must be successfully recognized in at least three separate frames (MIN_FRAMES_FOR_PRESENT = 3) during the first 15 minutes of lecture.
Liveness detection monitors eye blinking across consecutive frames to reject printed photos and screens.

questions.question: Walk through the enrollment procedure in your Face Recognition Module. How is an enrolled template generated for a student?
expected_points: Captures 20 images per student across multiple angles.
Aligns and resizes each captured image to 160x160 pixels.
Passes images through the embedding model and calculates the average embedding vector to serve as the template.

questions.question: How are face embeddings and biometric data secured and managed in your database schema to protect student privacy?
expected_points: Embeddings are isolated in a separate face_embeddings table encrypted with AES-256.
Access is restricted strictly to the API service account.
Raw face images are deleted immediately following enrollment, storing only mathematical embeddings.

questions.question: Explain the implementation and logic of the match_face function in face_matcher.py, including how cosine similarity is evaluated.
expected_points: Computes cosine similarity between input embedding and enrolled templates using the dot product divided by the product of vector norms.
Initializes threshold at SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD (0.75) and iterates through enrolled templates.
Returns the student_id with the highest similarity score strictly greater than the threshold, or None if none qualify.

questions.question: What trade-offs were observed when tuning the cosine similarity threshold to 0.75 on your validation dataset?
expected_points: Evaluated using a validation cohort of 40 students.
The chosen threshold of 0.75 resulted in a False Acceptance Rate (FAR) of 0.5 percent.
Yielded a False Rejection Rate (FRR) of 3 percent.

questions.question: How does your database maintain query performance under 100 milliseconds for semester-wide attendance reports?
expected_points: Indexes are placed specifically on student_id and session_id within the relational schema.
Attendance records reference student and lecture session keys with stored summary metrics (first seen time, recognised frame counts).

questions.question: Detail how the update_attendance logic in face_matcher.py determines when a student is officially marked present.
expected_points: Takes a counts dictionary and increments the recognition tally for the student_id.
Compares the updated count against MIN_FRAMES_FOR_PRESENT (set to 3).
Returns True to designate attendance only when count meets or exceeds 3 frames.
